source: Captured 2026-07-31 on GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest (workflow run 30604713594), the same runner class the gate executes on. The previous baseline was taken on a developer machine on 2026-02-08 and was not comparable: it reported +104% on xas_group_benchmark_single purely from host differences, while autobk_stage_linear_direct had in fact become ~12x faster than it recorded.
notes: Threshold widened from 10% to 25%. These are absolute timings on shared CI runners, so part of the run-to-run spread is host noise rather than signal: across two consecutive runs of identical code, xas_group_benchmark_parallel moved 4.8% (1424.873 -> 1492.776 ms) while xas_group_benchmark_single moved 0.29%. 25% leaves roughly 5x headroom over the observed spread while still catching a genuine 2x regression.
Re-capture this file from a CI run, never from a developer machine, or the comparison measures the host instead of the commit.
The durable fix is to benchmark the merge base and the head within a single job and compare relatively, which removes the dependency on a committed absolute baseline entirely.
